user.title: Powerline Network
user.description:
Click 'Submit' to scan for Powerline adapters on your network.

Requires raw socket access (CAP_NET_RAW).

Supports: TP-Link, FRITZ!Powerline, devolo, and other HomePlug AV adapters.

data_description.interface: 'auto' picks the first wired interface. Choose a specific one if your adapters live on another network segment (e.g. a VLAN interface).

confirm.title: Devices Found

probe.title: Remote probe
probe.description:
For adapters in another VLAN than Home Assistant. HomePlug is layer 2 and never routed, so a small probe in the adapters' network reads them and forwards only the values. Setup: see the README, section "Home Assistant in its own VLAN".

The probe is read-only: LED, power saving, QoS and restart cannot be switched through it.

data_description.probe_token: The same token the probe was started with (--token-file). Leave empty if it runs without one.

error.no_devices_found: No Powerline adapters found. Check that adapters are plugged in, paired, and connected via Ethernet cable. Home Assistant needs CAP_NET_RAW.
error.no_interface: No suitable network interface found. Make sure an Ethernet cable is connected.
error.probe_unreachable: Probe not reachable, or wrong token.

abort.already_configured: This Powerline network is already configured.
abort.raw_socket_unavailable:
Raw socket access not available. Home Assistant needs CAP_NET_RAW capability.

For Docker: use --cap-add=NET_RAW --network=host
For HAOS: install as add-on with host network
For venv: sudo setcap cap_net_raw+ep $(readlink -f $(which python3))

init.title: Powerline Network Options
init.description: Adjust polling behavior. Changes take effect immediately.

data.spatial_hub: Provide data to Spatial Hub (network layer on the floor plan)

alerts.link_slow_message: The connection **{source} ↔ {destination}** has been much slower than usual for {minutes} minutes: {average} Mbit/s (typical: ~{baseline} Mbit/s).
alerts.adapter_removed_message: Adapter **{name}** ({mac}) has disappeared from the powerline network and was removed from the topology.
alerts.adapter_new_message: New adapter **{name}** ({mac}) joined the powerline network.
alerts.cause_daily_interference: Possible cause: an electrical appliance may be disturbing the connection at recurring times of day.
alerts.action_check_noise_sources: Check whether a washing machine, refrigerator, or switching power supply runs at those times. Unplug suspected devices one at a time as a test.
alerts.cause_power_strip_or_filter: Possible cause: a power strip or surge protector may be attenuating the powerline signal.
alerts.action_use_wall_socket: As a test, plug both powerline adapters directly into wall outlets, not into a power strip or surge protector.
alerts.cause_directional_interference: Possible cause: a noise source or attenuation at one end may be affecting TX and RX differently.
alerts.action_check_both_ends: Check outlets and connected power supplies at both ends. Test the adapters directly in wall outlets and disconnect suspected appliances one at a time for comparison.
alerts.cause_phase_or_rcd: Possible cause: the adapters may be on different electrical phases or separated by an RCD/GFCI or filter element.
alerts.action_check_circuit_phase: Check whether both outlets are on the same circuit. Do not open electrical installations; have an electrician check the phase and RCD/GFCI if needed.
